About

I grew up in Panipat around my family’s yarn and fibre trading business. Being around that trade got me interested early in textiles, in manufacturing, and in how a business connects raw materials to finished products. I’m now doing the online BBA in Digital Business and Entrepreneurship at IIM Bangalore, where the first year covers marketing, entrepreneurship, finance and business communication.

Outside class I follow Indian financial markets and mutual funds, and I’m interested in how sourcing, production and trade fit together in manufacturing businesses. Longer term, I want to build a business in textile manufacturing and exports, starting with rugs, carpets and home furnishings.

Business mindset

I’m early in my career, so this is how I try to think rather than a record of results. Each point comes from something I’ve seen up close or studied.

  • Follow the whole chain

    Yarn, weaving or tufting, finishing, then the buyer. A problem usually starts a step before it shows up, so I try to trace a product back to its raw material before judging a cost or a delay.

    From: family yarn trade, operations internship

  • Start from the buyer

    A product that is easy to make but doesn’t match what a buyer needs doesn’t get reordered. I like to begin with what buyers ask for, such as material, size, price and delivery, and work back to the factory floor.

    From: buyer requirements, home furnishings focus

  • Don’t lean on one market

    About 60% of India’s home textile exports go to the US. I’d rather build for two or three markets from the start, and the UK has been open to Indian textiles duty-free since July 2026.

    From: the market figures below

  • Let the numbers decide

    I compare mutual fund schemes by looking at the figures rather than the headlines. I want to run a business the same way: cost each order properly before quoting it, and know what each product line really earns.

    From: mutual fund research, finance and statistics coursework

Where I’m headed

I want to build a textile manufacturing and export business, starting with rugs, carpets and home textiles.

Textile Manufacturing Home Furnishings International Trade

The market I’m looking at

  • 2,000+registered textile units in Panipat, mostly small and medium enterprises
  • ~30%of India’s home textile exports are carpets and rugs, by value
  • ~60%of India’s home textile exports go to one market, the US
  • 0%UK duty on Indian textiles since 15 July 2026, down from up to 12%

Panipat is a recognised Town of Export Excellence, and its units already sell rugs, carpets and other home textiles to buyers in Europe, the US and the Middle East. Demand is concentrated in one market, so I want to understand how finished home furnishings are sourced, costed and sold across several, not just how they are made.

Sources: CRISIL Ratings (US share), CRISIL via The Home Fashion (carpet share), Apparel Resources (Panipat units), PIB and FashionUnited (India–UK trade agreement). Figures as reported; checked November 2026.

What I want to learn next

  • How an export order works, from documentation and shipping terms to getting paid.
  • How to cost a rug or carpet, from raw material to freight.
  • What buyers in the US and UK look for in home furnishings.
  • Using Excel to model margins and working-capital needs.
